source.title: Mix & Match: training convnets with mixed image sizes for improved accuracy, speed and scale resiliency
source.authors: Elad Hoffer; Berry Weinstein; Itay Hubara; Tal Ben-Nun; T. Hoefler; Daniel Soudry

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether enlarged effective batch regimes change held-out accuracy under fixed epoch budgets, using mixed image sizes and batch augmentation rather than a direct large-batch comparison.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy for baseline, B+ and D+ regimes at fixed epoch budgets. The B+ and D+ conditions change image size and effective batch or duplicate count together; the study does not isolate batch size as the cause.
record.test_reason: The B+ experiments directly measure held-out accuracy with larger, varying batches at fixed epoch budgets under an adapted recipe. They bear on V5's allowance that recipe changes can remove the penalty. Image size, gradient smoothing, calibration and sometimes learning rate change together, so these results do not isolate batch size or test the unadapted large-batch penalty.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that stochastic mixed image and batch sizes offer fewer training iterations or improved classification accuracy, together with greater resilience to evaluation-image-size changes.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies image size together with batch size or batch-augmentation duplicates, and proposes gradient smoothing and batch-norm calibration; it does not directly replicate the cited large-batch generalization studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model affect the reported accuracy change; B+ and D+ regimes yield different outcomes. Evaluation image size also changes accuracy, but that is image-size resilience rather than the V5 batch-size comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed-size training improves accuracy across evaluation resolutions and allows smaller evaluation images at comparable accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training convolutional classifiers with mixed image sizes improves resilience to changes in evaluation resolution and can reduce inference computation.

record.problems: Batch size is confounded with image size and, in D+, batch augmentation; the comparisons therefore do not isolate the effect of large batch size. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional V5 table rows were omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps, zero-training-error thresholds, and test error beyond those thresholds.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.

The penalty under an unchanged recipe; batch-size thresholds; fixed large batches isolated from image size; longer-training recovery; language models; and the separate causal contributions of smoothing, image-size changes, learning-rate scaling and calibration.
Dropout addition, removal, strength, and interactions with training-set size or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: Record baseline/B+/D+ optimization-step counts alongside accuracy: 156K/109K/156K for ResNet-44 and WRN-28-10 CIFAR settings; 469K/328K/469K for AmoebaNet; 450K/169K/450K for ResNet-50; and 1000K/376K/1000K for EfficientNet-B0. These establish the reduced-step comparison and expose the unsupported AmoebaNet epoch assignment.

The gradient-smoothing ablation reports slightly improved final accuracy for ResNet-44 on CIFAR-10 with varying batch sizes. Add the qualitative result and its actual experimental conditions; numerical effect size cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

record.verdict_notes: States describe the direction relative to V5's batch penalty; absent or reversed penalties under adapted recipes support its adaptation clause. No reported condition establishes an unadapted penalty or challenges the qualified version. D+ enlarges batches through correlated augmentations without increasing the number of distinct examples per step. No uncertainty estimates are supplied. Section 5.2 reports 77.14% for an S(144) model at size 224, whereas Table 2 reports 78.04% for D+; the configurations are insufficiently distinguished to merge those values.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
The study does not isolate batch size from image size or batch augmentation, test language models, or compare large batches across workload-dependent sizes.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-measure comparison.
